problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,1]\times [-1,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=3x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-8xy-y.
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the pointt $[-1,\,-1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | {{field-1}} | $-14$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $-5$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-14$ | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-8xy-y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-8xy-y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}+6x-8y \\ 6xy-8x-1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}+6x-8y) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-8x-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}+6x-8y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy-8x-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 6y-8 \\ 6y-8 & 6x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6 & 6y-8 \\ 6y-8 & 6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}+6x-8y \\ 6xy-8x-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 6y-8 \\ 6y-8 & 6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}+6x-8y \\ 6xy-8x-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 6(-1)-8 \\ 6(-1)-8 & 6(-1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}3(-1)^{2}+6(-1)-8(-1) \\ 6(-1)(-1)-8(-1)-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -14 \\ -14 & -6\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -13\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function f:Rn→R is

xn+1=xn−[Hf(xn)]−1∇f(xn),

where H(xn) and ∇f(xn) are the Hessian and gradient of f, respectively, evaluated at xn.

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

Hf(xn)(xn+1−xn)=−∇f(xn).

In our case, the gradient is

∇f(x)=[∂∂x(3xy2+3x2−8xy−y)∂∂y(3xy2+3x2−8xy−y)]=[3y2+6x−8y6xy−8x−1],

and the Hessian is

Hf(x)=[∂∂x(3y2+6x−8y)∂∂x(6xy−8x−1)∂∂y(3y2+6x−8y)∂∂y(6xy−8x−1)]=[66y−86y−86x].

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

[66y−86y−86x]xn(xn+1−xn)=−[3y2+6x−8y6xy−8x−1]xn.

Starting with x0=[−1−1], we have

[66y−86y−86x]x0(x1−x0)=−[3y2+6x−8y6xy−8x−1]x0[66(−1)−86(−1)−86(−1)](x1−x0)=−[3(−1)2+6(−1)−8(−1)6(−1)(−1)−8(−1)−1][6−14−14−6](x1−x0)=[−5−13].
